decision.basis: Remove the binding value-cell forwarding layer while retaining the same graph nodes, readiness preparation, cleanup, error routing and callback arities. Allocation sampling decreases and forced-GC live page memory after 1k rows decreases 3.20%; complete CPU comparisons do not establish a stable overall speed improvement.
decision.tradeoffs: Pooled 1k creation is 0.56% slower and append is 1.07% slower. The two complete CPU rounds have opposite overall directions. The five-framework 1.10 target is not evaluated here.
rejectedClaims: Do not infer overall CPU improvement from fewer closures or the pooled point estimate.
Do not reintroduce the historically rejected row-ID elimination or class/label fusion prototypes without new current-stack evidence.

method.cpu: Official nine CPU cases, 15 samples except selection 25, default harness slowdown: 4x partial update/select/swap/clear, 2x remove, 1x create/replace/append.
method.roundA: One complete invocation for both entries; harness order baseline then prepared within each case, cases 01 through 09.
method.roundB: Separate invocations in reverse case order 09 through 01, prepared then baseline within every case.
method.memory: Separate official 21/22/25 page-memory workloads, three samples per entry and case after forced GC. Values are MiB, not JS heap-only bytes.
method.isolation: No builds, tests, other profiling or other timing runs overlap the CPU or memory batches. Profiles run separately from each other and from timing.
method.uncertainty: Report both complete rounds and all samples. The pooled geometric ratio is descriptive and does not establish a causal speed win or a general runtime cost model.

method.scope: Diagnostic sampling with profiler overhead; never included in benchmark scores. CPU capture includes the target click and two animation frames. Allocation estimates include garbage collected during capture and do not represent retained heap or whole-page memory.
